# Employment Offer Letter Creation Guide

## 1. Skill Purpose

This skill provides templates and patterns for creating legally sound employment documentation. For your request, you will primarily draw on:

- **Template 1: Offer Letter** — the pre-hire document extending the job offer
- **Template 3: Employee Handbook Policy** — useful for referencing benefits, PTO, and code of conduct details
- **Core legal concepts** — at-will vs. contract, exempt vs. non-exempt classification, jurisdiction-specific rules

> **⚠️ IMPORTANT DISCLAIMER:** These templates are for informational purposes only and do not constitute legal advice. Consult with qualified legal counsel before using any employment documents, particularly for engineering roles involving IP, confidentiality, and non-compete clauses.

---

## 2. Employment Document Types Overview

| Document | Purpose | When Used |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| **Offer Letter** (this request) | Initial job offer | Pre-hire |
| **Employment Contract** | Formal agreement | Hire |
| **Employee Handbook** | Policies & procedures | Onboarding |
| **NDA** | Confidentiality | Before access to code/IP |
| **Non-Compete** | Competition restriction | Hire/Exit |

**Legal classification framework:**
```
Employment Relationship:
├── At-Will vs. Contract
├── Employee vs. Contractor       ← Critical for engineers
├── Full-Time vs. Part-Time
├── Exempt vs. Non-Exempt         ← Critical for salary determination
└── Jurisdiction-Specific Requirements
```

---

## 3. Workflow for Creating an Offer Letter

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ STEP 1: Gather Position Details                                 │
│   - Job title, department, reporting structure                  │
│   - Location / remote status                                    │
│   - Start date, employment type (full-time/contract)            │
│   - Exempt vs. non-exempt classification                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ STEP 2: Determine Compensation Package                          │
│   - Base salary (benchmark against local market)                │
│   - Bonus eligibility and percentage                            │
│   - Equity (stock options/RSUs; vesting schedule)               │
│   - Sign-on bonus (if applicable)                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ STEP 3: Reference Benefits & Policies                           │
│   - Health insurance effective dates                            │
│   - 401(k) match                                                │
│   - PTO / holidays                                              │
│   - Remote work equipment stipend (if applicable for engineers) │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ STEP 4: List Contingencies                                      │
│   - Background check                                            │
│   - Right to work verification                                  │
│   - Required documents: NDA, IP Assignment, Non-Compete         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ STEP 5: Include At-Will / Contract Status                       │
│   - Verify state law (CA, NY, etc. have specific requirements)   │
│   - Include at-will language where applicable                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ STEP 6: Customize Role-Specific Sections for Engineers          │
│   - IP assignment emphasis                                      │
│   - Remote work / on-call expectations (if any)                 │
│   - Security & confidentiality requirements                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ STEP 7: Legal Review & Send                                     │
│   - Have HR and legal counsel review                            │
│   - Issue with acceptance deadline                              │
│   - File executed copy                                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 4. Offer Letter Template (Tailored for Senior Software Engineer)

Below is the offer letter template, with inline annotations **[ENGINEERING NOTE]** highlighting areas to customize for a senior software engineer hire:

```markdown
# EMPLOYMENT OFFER LETTER

[Company Letterhead]

Date: [DATE]

[Candidate Name]
[Address]
[City, State ZIP]

Dear [Candidate Name],

We are pleased to extend an offer of employment for the position of Senior
Software Engineer at [COMPANY NAME]. We believe your skills and experience
will be valuable additions to our team.

## Position Details

**Title:** Senior Software Engineer
**Department:** [Engineering / Product / Technology]
**Reports To:** [VP of Engineering / Engineering Manager]
**Location:** [Office Location / Remote / Hybrid — specify expected % on-site]
**Start Date:** [Proposed Start Date]
**Employment Type:** Full-Time, [Exempt / Non-Exempt]

[ENGINEERING NOTE: Senior Software Engineers are typically classified as
EXEMPT under the FLSA "computer professional" exemption. Confirm with legal
counsel that salary meets the minimum threshold for your state.]

## Compensation

**Base Salary:** $[AMOUNT] per year, paid [bi-weekly/semi-monthly].
**Bonus:** Eligible for an annual performance bonus of up to [15–25]% of base
salary, based on individual and [company/team] performance. Bonus is
discretionary and requires active employment at payment date.
**Equity:** Subject to Board approval, you will be granted [X] stock options
(or RSUs) under the Company's 2024 Equity Incentive Plan, vesting over 4 years
with a 1-year cliff. Full terms in a separate Stock Option Agreement / RSU
Agreement.
**[Sign-On Bonus:** $[AMOUNT], subject to repayment if you voluntarily resign
within [12] months of start date — OPTIONAL, if offered.]

[ENGINEERING NOTE: Equity language is critical for senior engineering
hires. Be precise about: option type (ISO/NSO vs RSU), number of shares,
exercise price, vesting schedule (4-year / 1-year cliff is standard), and
existence of accelerated vesting clauses (e.g., double-trigger on acquisition).]

## Benefits

You will be eligible for our standard benefits package, effective [date]:
- Health insurance (medical, dental, vision)
- 401(k) with [X]% company match
- [X] days paid time off per year ([note if unlimited PTO])
- [X] paid holidays + [floating holidays]
- [Remote work stipend: $X one-time home office equipment budget]  ← For remote engineers
- [Professional development budget: $X/year for conferences/courses]  ← Optional
- [Other benefits: parental leave, wellness stipend, etc.]

Full details will be provided during onboarding.

## Intellectual Property and Confidentiality

[ENGINEERING NOTE: For software engineers, this section is essential. The
candidate will likely sign a separate IP Assignment Agreement and NDA at hire.
The offer letter should reference these documents explicitly.]

This offer is contingent upon your execution of required employment
documents including:
- Confidentiality Agreement (covering proprietary source code, trade secrets,
  architecture, internal tools, and product roadmap)
- Intellectual Property Assignment Agreement (all code and inventions created
  within the scope of employment are assigned to the Company)
- [Non-Compete Agreement, if applicable and enforceable in your state]
- [Outside Activities Disclosure — if the engineer maintains open-source
  projects or a side business, review for conflicts]

**Prior Inventions:** Please attach a list of any prior inventions, open-source
projects, or other work developed outside of employment that you wish to
exclude from the IP Assignment Agreement. [Exhibit A]

## Contingencies

This offer is contingent upon:
- Successful completion of background check
- Verification of your right to work in [Country]
- Execution of all required employment documents listed above

## Remote Work / On-Call Expectations  [MODIFY AS APPLICABLE]

- [Fully remote within [state/country] OR hybrid: 3 days/week in office]
- [Expected on-call rotation: 1 week per month, compensated per policy OR no
  scheduled on-call]

[ENGINEERING NOTE: If on-call is expected, specify compensation or time-off
policy here or reference the engineering handbook policy. Ambiguity here is a
common source of disputes.]

## At-Will Employment

Please note that employment with [Company Name] is at-will. This means that
either you or the Company may terminate the employment relationship at any
time, with or without cause or notice. This offer letter does not constitute
a contract of employment for any specific period.

[ENGINEERING NOTE: At-will language applies in most US states except Montana.
Some states (CA) strictly limit or prohibit non-competes — consult counsel
before inserting one.]

## Acceptance

To accept this offer, please sign below and return by [DEADLINE DATE —
typically 5–10 business days]. This offer will expire if not accepted by that
date.

We are excited about the possibility of you joining [Engineering Team Name].
If you have any questions, please contact [HR Contact] at [email/phone].

Sincerely,

_________________________
[Hiring Manager / CTO Name]
[Title]
[Company Name]

---

## ACCEPTANCE

I accept this offer of employment and agree to the terms stated above.

Signature: _________________________

Printed Name: _________________________

Date: _________________________

Anticipated Start Date: _________________________

---

## EXHIBIT A: PRIOR INVENTIONS & OUTSIDE ACTIVITIES  [Include if applicable]

[Engineer to list prior inventions, open-source contributions, side projects,
or write "None"]

_________________________
```

---

## 5. Best Practices for This Document

### Do's
- **Consult legal counsel** — engineering compensation and IP clauses are jurisdiction-sensitive (especially CA restrictions on non-competes vs. states like TX or FL that permit them)
- **Customize by jurisdiction** — never send a copy-paste generic letter
- **Be precise on equity** — exact vesting, cliff, exercise period, and option type
- **Reference but don't restate the full IP agreement** — the letter should point to the separate agreements, not replace them
- **Allow time for engineering-specific negotiations** — senior engineers often negotiate equity, remote policy, sign-on bonus, and start date; build slack into the deadline
- **Keep a signed copy** in the personnel file / HRIS before the start date

### Don'ts
- **Don't create an implied contract** — avoid language promising continued employment, specific duration, or guaranteed future raises
- **Don't promise bonus amounts as guaranteed** — always frame discretionary bonuses as at company discretion
- **Don't omit at-will language** — in at-will states, this is critical
- **Don't skip the Prior Inventions / outside activities discussion** — a failure to exclude prior work before hire commonly causes legal disputes over ownership after the engineer joins
- **Don't draft non-competes without state-specific counsel** — enforceability varies wildly, and CA, NY, WA, and CO have materially different rules
- **Don't send before internal approval** — verify comp band, budget, and available headcount are signed off

---

## 6. Related Documentation to Draft Next (Workflow Continuation)

Once the offer letter is accepted, the documentation workflow continues with:

1. **Employment Agreement / Contract** (if not at-will, or for executives) — Template 2 in this skill
2. **NDA** — required before the engineer gets code access
3. **IP Assignment Agreement** — required before the engineer writes any code
4. **Employee Handbook Acknowledgment** — required at onboarding (Template 3)
5. **State-specific notices** — e.g., California pay transparency notices, paid sick leave notices, which cannot be covered by generic templates

**Resources referenced by the skill for ongoing updates:**
- [SHRM Employment Templates](https://www.shrm.org/)
- [Department of Labor](https://www.dol.gov/)
- [EEOC Guidance](https://www.eeoc.gov/)
- State-specific labor departments

---

## Summary of Next Steps

1. Fill in the income/equity data and engineering-specific sections above
2. Confirm the **exempt classification** and salary threshold with HR
3. Prepare or attach the **Prior Inventions exhibit** for the candidate to fill out
4. Have legal counsel review the letter and the companion IP/NDA documents
5. Route through internal approval, then issue with a clear expiration date
